title: Total Letter Jumps
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. Walking from left to right, each step from one letter to the next is a jump whose length is the absolute difference of the two letters' character codes. For example, the jump from "c" to "a" has length 2, and so does the jump from "a" to "c".

Return the total length of all jumps between neighboring letters.

examples.why: c → a is 2, a → b is 1.
Three jumps of 2. Comparing only the first and last letter would give 0: every step counts, including the ones that go back.
Equal neighbors are a jump of length 0.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Each jump depends only on two neighboring letters. How many jumps are there in a string of length n?
There are n − 1 jumps. Look at pairs (s[i − 1], s[i]) for i from 1 to n − 1.
Add Math.abs(s.charCodeAt(i) − s.charCodeAt(i − 1)) for every i ≥ 1.

explain.intuition:
The total is a sum over neighboring pairs, and each pair is independent of the others. So one pass that looks at s[i − 1] and s[i] is all you need. Letters are compared by their character codes, the same numbers charCodeAt returns.

The absolute value matters: a step back down the alphabet is just as long as a step up. Without it, steps cancel and the sum collapses to last − first.
steps: For i from 1 to n − 1, add |code(s[i]) − code(s[i − 1])| to total.
pitfalls: Dropping the absolute value. The signed differences telescope to code(last) − code(first), which is wrong for "acac".
Starting the loop at 0 and reading s[-1], which is undefined in JavaScript and the last letter in Python.

solutions.title: One pass over neighboring pairs
solutions.idea: Walk i from 1 and add the absolute difference of the codes of s[i − 1] and s[i].

solutions.title: Codes first, then differences
solutions.idea: Turn the string into an array of codes, then sum the absolute differences of neighbors. Same idea, written as two simple passes.

followups: You may reorder the letters freely. Which order gives the largest total, and which the smallest?
Answer many queries asking for the total of the substring s[l..r]. What would you precompute?
